title: Derived Hom Mayer–Vietoris for elementary distinguished squares of spaces
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $W$ an algebraic space over $S$ with its small etale structure sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and canonical derived tensor pullback $Lh^*$ from [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], computed by K-flat resolutions. Let $(U\subset W,p:V\to W)$ be an elementary distinguished square: $U$ is an open subspace [def-a1-space-open-subspace], $p$ is representable etale, and $V\times_W Z\to Z$ is an isomorphism for the reduced closed subspace $Z$ with underlying set $|W|\setminus|U|$ [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support, def-a1-space-point-topology]. Put $T=U\times_WV$. For $E,F\in D(\mathcal O_W)$, let $E_A,F_A$ denote their exact etale restrictions for $A=U,V,T$, and put $\operatorname{Ext}_A^n(E_A,F_A)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_A)}(E_A,F_A[n])$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. There is a long exact sequence
$$\cdots\to\operatorname{Ext}_T^{n-1}(E_T,F_T)\xrightarrow{\partial}\operatorname{Ext}_W^n(E,F)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}_U^n(E_U,F_U)\oplus\operatorname{Ext}_V^n(E_V,F_V)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}_T^n(E_T,F_T)\xrightarrow{\partial}\operatorname{Ext}_W^{n+1}(E,F)\to\cdots.$$
The middle maps are restriction and difference of restrictions. The boundary is the one obtained by applying derived Hom into $F$ to the canonical extension-by-zero triangle associated to the exact sequence of [lem-sfb-space-elementary-shriek-exact]. The sequence is natural contravariantly in $E$ and covariantly in $F$. For every morphism $h:W'\to W$, base change gives an elementary distinguished square on $W'$, and the canonical pullback maps on every displayed Ext group, using derived pullback composition and shift isomorphisms, form a morphism to the long exact sequence for $Lh^*E,Lh^*F$ on that square; in particular they commute with the specified boundaries. No boundedness, quasi-coherence, flatness or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08H9 (lemma-mayer-vietoris-hom), including its proof from lemma-exact-sequence-lower-shriek; base-change naturality uses the same canonical extension-by-zero sequence, whose base-changed form is recorded in lem-sfb-space-elementary-shriek-exact.

proof.text: Write $J_A=j_{A!}j_A^*$ for $A=U,V,T$. The exact additive functors and signed natural maps of [lem-sfb-space-elementary-shriek-exact] give, on every complex $C$, a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to J_TC\xrightarrow d J_UC\oplus J_VC\xrightarrow e C\to0$. Their termwise functors descend, with their shift maps, by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to obtain the distinguished triangle $J_TE\xrightarrow d J_UE\oplus J_VE\xrightarrow e E\xrightarrow{\delta_E}J_TE[1]$. This is the canonical short-exact-sequence triangle, natural in $E$: naturality on complexes descends through localization, whose fully faithful precomposition property is [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property].

For each $A$, the specified exact adjunction $j_{A!}\dashv j_A^*$ is part of [lem-sfb-space-elementary-shriek-exact]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] and then [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization], using the factorizations of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. This gives $\operatorname{Hom}(j_{A!}M,F[n])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,j_A^*F[n])$ for arbitrary derived $M,F$ and all integers $n$. The derived counit is the localized evaluation counit. These adjunction bijections respect shifts: the termwise unit and counit have degree zero, so shifting their components changes neither map, while additivity preserves the signed differential $(-1)^nd$. Thus no boundedness is needed for this adjunction.

source.place: Tag 08FJ (lemma-adjoint-lower-shriek-restrict); derived.tex Tag 015F; normalized localization adjunction

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] to the triangle of step 1 and its successive rotations with target $F[n]$. Rotation and integral shifts are those of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. The two exactness assertions, for all rotations, give exactness at every term of the resulting long sequence. Identify the three local terms by step 2, and identify $\operatorname{Hom}(J_UE\oplus J_VE,F[n])$ with the pair of Hom groups by its two components. Explicitly, if $a:J_TE\to F[n]$ is the adjoint of an element of $\operatorname{Ext}_T^n(E_T,F_T)$, its connecting image is $a[1]\circ\delta_E:E\to F[n+1]$, using the standard shift identifications. This defines precisely the specified boundary and gives the displayed sequence in every integer degree.

The map induced by $e$ sends $f:E\to F[n]$ to its restrictions: its $A$ component is $f\circ\varepsilon_{A,E}$, whose adjoint is $j_A^*f$ by the adjunction triangle identity. For $T\to A$, precomposing the adjoint $j_{A!}E_A\to F[n]$ with the overlap counit gives the adjoint of its restriction to $T$: on the sum presheaf both composites evaluate each nested summand in $F$, then the equality localizes. The signs $(+,-)$ of $d$ therefore give restriction from $U$ minus restriction from $V$. This uses the counit description in [lem-sfb-space-elementary-shriek-exact] and the normalization of [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization]. For $x:E'\to E$, naturality of step 1 says $J_Tx[1]\delta_{E'}=\delta_Ex$; hence $(aJ_Tx)[1]\delta_{E'}=(a[1]\delta_E)x$. For $y:F\to F'$, $(y[n]a)[1]\delta_E=y[n+1](a[1]\delta_E)$. These equations prove naturality of the boundary, and the restriction maps are natural by composition.

source.place: Tag 08H9, signed arrows from Tag 08GV; sites-modules.tex Tag 03DI evaluation on nested summands

proof.text: For an arbitrary $h:W'\to W$, [lem-sfb-space-elementary-shriek-exact] supplies the base-changed exact functors and their same signed maps, with the reduced complement taken on $W'$. In particular this is the elementary square on $W'$ stipulated there. This does not presume that the old reduced complement stays reduced. More explicitly, [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] identifies the support of $Z\times_WW'$ with the complement of $U'$; the reduced closed subspace $Z'$ of that support factors through $Z\times_WW'$. On reduced etale scheme charts, every element of its defining ideal vanishes at all points and hence is nilpotent, therefore zero. Base changing $V\times_WZ\cong Z$ to $Z'$ gives $V'\times_{W'}Z'\cong Z'$. The restrictions in this comparison satisfy $j_A'^*Lh^*\cong Lh_A^*j_A^*$, with canonical composition, by [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus].

Choose a flat-term K-flat complex $P$ representing $E$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-sfb-space-etale-sum-pullback], all $J_AP$ are K-flat with flat terms. Put $A=J_TP$, $B=J_UP\oplus J_VP$ and $C=P$. Their cone $D=C(d:A\to B)$ and $B$ are K-flat by [lem-sfb-kflat-homotopy-triangulated]. Its hypotheses hold for module sheaves: [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] supplies additive symmetric closed tensor, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] supplies small colimits; tensor preserves them because its adjunction carries the colimit universal property to the limit of the Hom sets. Symmetry identifies the two-sided K-flat condition with [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The cone terms are $B^r\oplus A^{r+1}$ and are flat: tensoring with a finite direct sum is the sum of the two exact tensor functors. Consequently $A,B,C,D$ all compute their derived pullbacks by ordinary $h^*$, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback].

The comparisons of [lem-sfb-space-etale-sum-pullback], composed with the restriction comparisons of [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus], identify $h^*J_AP$ with $J_A'(h^*P)$. They preserve the nested counits and finite sums, so they give an isomorphism of three-term sequences of complexes, including $d$ and $e$, from $h^*$ of the sequence $0\to J_TP\to J_UP\oplus J_VP\to P\to0$ to the sequence of step 5 evaluated on $h^*P$. The latter is short exact by step 5, although $h^*$ need not be exact on arbitrary sequences. By step 6 all three terms of the sequence on $W$ are K-flat with flat terms, so [lem-sfb-ringed-kflat-pullback-ses-triangle] applies: the comparisons $\epsilon$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] form an isomorphism of triangles from $Lh^*$ of the canonical triangle of step 1 (its last arrow followed by the shift comparison of $Lh^*$) to the canonical triangle of the termwise pulled-back sequence, including the boundary; explicitly, additivity of $h^*$ identifies $h^*\operatorname{Cone}(d)$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(h^*d)$ (terms $h^*B^r\oplus h^*A^{r+1}$, differential entries $h^*d_B,h^*d,-h^*d_A$), carrying $h^*q,h^*p$ to the cone maps $q',p'$, and the boundaries are $-pq^{-1}$ and $-p'(q')^{-1}$. Naturality of canonical triangles [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] for the isomorphism of short exact sequences above then gives an isomorphism to the canonical triangle of step 1 on $W'$ for $h^*P$, which represents $Lh^*E$. Thus the three specified comparison isomorphisms form an isomorphism from $Lh^*$ of the triangle in step 1 to the canonical triangle for $Lh^*E$, including its last arrow.

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), formula and functorial cone computation; spaces-perfect.tex Tag 08GV

proof.text:
Let $L=Lh^*$ and let $c_A:LJ_AE\xrightarrow{\sim}J_A'LE$ be step 7's comparisons. Pulling a morphism $f:E\to F[n]$ through $L$, followed by the shift comparison, defines the global Ext pullback. On the local terms it is precisely $Lh_A^*$: the sum-extension comparison preserves evaluation counits [lem-sfb-space-etale-sum-pullback], and [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] identifies adjoints using those counits. Thus taking the transpose before or after pullback gives the same morphism on the slice, with the pullback composition identifications from [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus]. For $a:J_TE\to F[n]$, write $a'$ for $L(a)c_T^{-1}$ with the shift comparison. Step 7 says $\delta_{LE}=c_T[1]L(\delta_E)$, where shifts are understood canonically. Hence
$$a'[1]\delta_{LE}=L(a)[1]c_T^{-1}[1]c_T[1]L(\delta_E)=L(a[1]\delta_E).$$
This is the required boundary square. The squares for the two middle arrows follow from the preserved signed counits. It proves compatibility of the specified Ext pullback maps with the full long exact sequences, without a flatness, quasi-compactness, or boundedness assumption.
